images.title: Even last digits
images.purpose: Show that multiples of 2 end in 2, 4, 6, 8 or 0.
images.composition: One evenly spaced row of 5 round chips with a single label centred below.
images.exact_structure: One row of 5 equal amber #E69F00 circles evenly spaced holding 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. The last digit of each number is reddish purple #CC79A7. Exactly 5 circles, 1 line below.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any circle holding a number other than 2, 4, 6, 8, 10
images.description: Five circles showing 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 with each last digit highlighted.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to read the highlighted digits aloud and say which digits can end an even number.

image_decisions.why: A short row of multiples with highlighted last digits carries the idea.
